zip is compiled into ddtrace's Rust extension (ddtrace/internal/native/_native). The flaw is a skipped HMAC check when the reader of an AES-encrypted entry reaches EOF early, in the AES reader that ZipArchive uses to read entries. The shipped extension uses the ZipWriter path only; it contains no ZipArchive, ZipStreamReader or src/read code.

zip is compiled into ddtrace's Rust extension (ddtrace/internal/native/_native). The flaw is an unbounded allocation for symlink targets in ZipArchive::extract_internal (src/read). The shipped extension uses the ZipWriter path only; it contains no ZipArchive, ZipStreamReader or src/read code.

zip is compiled into ddtrace's Rust extension (ddtrace/internal/native/_native). The flaw is a mismatch between central-directory and local-header file names when ZipStreamReader extracts (src/read/stream.rs). The shipped extension uses the ZipWriter path only; it contains no ZipArchive, ZipStreamReader or src/read code.

zip is compiled into ddtrace's Rust extension (ddtrace/internal/native/_native). The flaw is in the symlink handling of ZipArchive::extract (src/read.rs). The shipped extension uses the ZipWriter path only; it contains no extraction code.

zip is compiled into ddtrace's Rust extension (ddtrace/internal/native/_native). The flaw keeps SUID/SGID bits in ZipArchive::extract and the stream extraction API (src/read.rs, src/read/stream.rs). The shipped extension uses the ZipWriter path only; it contains no extraction code.

zip is compiled into ddtrace's Rust extension (ddtrace/internal/native/_native). The flaw is in ZipArchive::extract and ZipStreamReader::extract (src/read.rs, src/read/stream.rs). The shipped extension uses the ZipWriter path only; it contains no ZipArchive, ZipStreamReader or src/read code.

This advisory flags the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package, which has no fixed version. This image's Go binaries do not include openpgp; the agent's OpenPGP support comes from a separate, maintained package.

RUSTSEC-2024-0449 is an informational notice that the unsafe-libyaml crate is unmaintained (repository archived 2024-03-25) and names no vulnerability and no patched release beyond 0.2.11. It comes into ddtrace's Rust extension through serde_yaml 0.9.34, which libdatadog's library-config crate uses. Replacing it needs an upstream libdatadog change.

RUSTSEC-2025-0141 is an informational notice that the bincode crate is unmaintained and names no vulnerability and no patched release; its authors consider 1.3.3 complete. bincode 1.3.3 comes into ddtrace's Rust extension through libdatadog's IPC library. Replacing it needs an upstream libdatadog change.

RUSTSEC-2024-0436 is an informational notice that the paste crate is unmaintained and names no vulnerability and no patched release. paste is a compile-time procedural macro that libdatadog's libunwind bindings use while ddtrace's Rust extension is built; it runs only at build time. Replacing it needs an upstream libdatadog change.

pyo3 is compiled into the Rust extensions of bcrypt 5.0.0, jellyfish 1.2.1, ddtrace 4.15.7 and pydantic-core 2.46.5. The flaw is a missing Sync bound on the closures that PyCFunction::new_closure accepts. None of these extensions calls PyCFunction::new_closure.

pyo3 0.28.3 is compiled into the Rust extensions of ddtrace 4.15.7 and pydantic-core 2.46.5. The flaw is an unchecked index in the PyList and PyTuple iterator nth and nth_back methods, which wraps only when the iterator's position plus n overflows usize. ddtrace calls nth only on Rust string splits. pydantic-core reaches PyTuple nth only through args.iter().enumerate().skip(count) on a fresh iterator, so the position is 0 and n is the schema's positional parameter count, which the code checks against the tuple length first. No extension calls nth_back.

pyo3 0.26.0 is compiled into the Rust extensions of bcrypt 5.0.0 and jellyfish 1.2.1. The flaw is an unchecked index in the PyList and PyTuple iterator nth and nth_back methods. Neither extension calls nth, nth_back, skip or step_by on a PyList or PyTuple iterator; jellyfish's only skip is on a Rust Vec<char>.

lru 0.16.3 is compiled into pydantic-core 2.46.5's Rust extension. The flaw is a missing detach in LruCache::pop when the key's Drop panics (https://github.com/jeromefroe/lru-rs/pull/238). pydantic-core's only LruCache is its regex cache, an LruCache<String, Regex> that it reads with get and fills with get_or_insert. It never calls pop, and a String key's Drop does not panic.

This CVE is a plugin search path problem in the Docker CLI plugin manager on Windows (the cli-plugins/manager package). This image runs on Linux and links only the Docker CLI configuration and credentials packages (cli/config), not the plugin manager, so none of the affected code is present.

This CVE is a privilege check error in the Docker daemon's plugin install logic and is scoped to the daemon's own code, which runs only inside dockerd. This image links an unrelated utility package from the same Go module but ships no Docker daemon and none of the affected code.

This CVE is a race in the Docker daemon's docker cp mount setup and is scoped to the daemon's own code, which runs only inside dockerd. This image links an unrelated utility package from the same Go module but ships no Docker daemon and none of the affected code.

This CVE lets the Docker daemon write a container's files to the host during archive extraction and is scoped to the daemon's own code, which runs only inside dockerd. This image links an unrelated utility package from the same Go module but ships no Docker daemon and none of the affected code.

This CVE affects the Docker daemon's handling of docker cp bind mounts and is scoped to the daemon's own code, which runs only inside dockerd. This image links an unrelated utility package from the same Go module but ships no Docker daemon and none of the affected code.

RUSTSEC-2026-0247 is an informational notice that the bitmaps crate is unmaintained (repository archived 2026-05-03) and names no vulnerability and no patched release. bitmaps 3.2.1 comes into ddtrace's Rust extension through libdatadog's profiling library; replacing it needs an upstream libdatadog change.

bitmaps 3.2.1 is compiled into ddtrace's Rust extension (ddtrace/internal/native/_native) through libdatadog's profiling library. The flaw is that Bitmap::try_from(&[u8]) and the AsMut<[u8]> implementation can write a byte that is not a valid bool into a Bitmap<1>. The only Bitmap in the extension is a Bitmap<32> in the profiler's upscaling rules, whose backing store is a u32; the code creates it with Default and uses only set and get.

DHI backport of upstream gh-150751 (python/cpython commits 2eb2af805c156ca52b316bb4ced5e0ab3971d0ae and 9f52b443c002cccfb54bda0706a9276b6b4a109d) applied to 3.10.22 through 3.15.2. http.client validates the Content-Length header as decimal digits only (RFC 9112 1*DIGIT), ignoring optional spaces or tabs around the value; a value with a sign, an underscore, or an embedded space is not used as the body length. Chunk sizes are validated as hexadecimal digits (RFC 9112 1*HEXDIG, 0-9, a-f and A-F), so valid upper- and lower-case hex chunk sizes are accepted, while a sign, a 0x prefix, an underscore or leading whitespace is rejected instead of being parsed with int(value, 16).

Debian security tracker: fixed in unstable by the same change as CVE-2026-85091, which is upstream zlib commit df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148. That change resets the stream input pointer and available input after a failed write() in gz_write(), so a later gz* write cannot use the stale caller buffer. This package build includes an adaptation of that upstream change for the zlib 1.3.1 code base. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-76844

statements.action_statement: Use-after-free in xmlParseInternalSubset (DoS via crafted XML with improper entity resolution) affecting libxml2 2.9.11-2.11.0. The DHI package ships the Debian trixie 2.9.14 repack, which is in the affected range. Upstream fixed this only as a side effect of the entity-amplification rework in https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/463bbeeca1805b5c4828f50d0fefc4eebaf620df (v2.11.0): a large parser.c rewrite plus ABI-changing additions to the public entities.h and parser.h structures. There is no isolated upstream patch, and neither Debian nor Ubuntu ships a backport to their 2.9.x branches. The fix cannot be applied to the 2.9.14 source without breaking API/ABI version compatibility for consumers, so no patch is carried. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6653

statements.status_notes: Uncontrolled recursion in xmlParseSGMLCatalog reachable only when a local user parses an untrusted SGML catalog with the xmlcatalog CLI. Both Debian (unimportant) and upstream consider this negligible (using untrusted SGML catalogs makes no sense). The upstream recursion-depth fix targets libxml2 2.15 catalog.c and does not apply to the trixie 2.9.14 source without invasive multi-function changes for a negligible CLI-only issue. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-8732

Integer underflow and heap out-of-bounds read in berval2tl_data() in the LDAP KDB backend plugin (plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c). Triggering requires a KDC or kadmind configured with an LDAP database backend whose backend returns a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2; that data originates from the trusted KDB datastore, not from an external Kerberos protocol client, so it cannot be controlled by an adversary. Debian marks this unimportant (bug 1139821) with no security impact and notes it does not cross any security boundary.
